key_insight: On EBench, combining GPT-6-Astra with post-trained robot policies matches the strongest compared policies overall while substantially reducing token cost.
engineering_relevance: Robot-control harnesses can combine a frontier model’s short-horizon strengths with specialized policies for longer, precise manipulation tasks.
method: Evaluate GPT-6-Astra on EBench using the same visual and proprioceptive observation protocol as post-trained policies.
Compare direct waypoint control with a harness that can invoke vision-language-action or world action model policies.
Assess task success across manipulation demands and generalization dimensions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports competitive direct-control performance, short-horizon leadership, and the least variation across generalization dimensions, but weaker long-horizon, tabletop, and high-precision contact-rich performance; no numerical results are provided.
watch_item: Hybrid performance remains below the per-task upper bound of standalone components because of suboptimal policy invocation, fixed-instruction execution without subgoals, and grasp disruption when agent control resumes.
paper_title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
